_note: Mail the company sends and receives that is not a customer enquiry: order notes, supplier traffic, newsletters, press, junk, pitches and mail between staff. Slots in braces. Brand voice: plain, exact, dry. No exclamation marks.

footnotes: ¹ Thank you for reading this far.
¹ Every order is checked twice. The second time is for fun.
¹ This email was written by a person, once, and reused.
¹ We do not send adverts in confirmations.
¹ Replies to this go to a real inbox.
¹ The small print is on the website, in a readable size.

Dear Mr Fezziwig,

I hope I am not troubling you. The figures for the week to {week}: {orders} orders, takings {revenue}, refunds {refunds}. Everything is entered and checked, I believe.

Yours, B. Cratchit

Dear Mr Fezziwig,

Week to {week}. Orders: {orders}. Takings: {revenue}. Refunds: {refunds}. I have checked them twice, and Mr Scrooge once.

Bob Cratchit

Mr Fezziwig,

Here are the figures for the week to {week}. {orders} orders came to {revenue}; {refunds} went back in refunds. Please tell me if anything looks odd.

B. Cratchit

Dear Mr Fezziwig,

Week to {week}: {orders} orders, {revenue} taken, {refunds} refunded. I am sorry it is not later; I wanted to be sure.

Bob

Dear Mr Fezziwig,

The week to {week} in short: {orders} orders, {revenue} in, {refunds} out in refunds. The books agree with the bank.

Yours, Bob Cratchit
replies:
Thank you, Bob. {orders} orders for the week to {week}, and {revenue} taken. Very good. Go home on time tonight, please.

Fezziwig

Many thanks, Bob. {orders} orders is a fine thing to read on a Monday. Put the kettle on.

Fezziwig

Thank you. {revenue} for the week to {week}. All well. I'll tell the others.

Fezziwig

Capital, Bob. Thank you for being so careful with the {orders}.

Fezziwig

Fezziwig

Fezziwig

Thank you, Bob. I have read the figures for {week}. They are in good order, which is thanks to you.

Fezziwig

Good, good. {orders} orders in the week to {week}. Please tell Mr Scrooge I said it was well done, and then please leave before he answers.

Fezziwig

Thank you. Another careful week, to {week}. I shall mention it at the meeting.

Fezziwig

Noted with thanks. {revenue}. A cup of tea is on its way to your desk.

Cratchit,

Entry {ref}: {amount} for {what}. Why? I should like it explained by the end of the day.

Scrooge

Bob,

I see {amount} against {what} ({ref}). Is that right? It looks like more than last time.

E. Scrooge

Cratchit,

{what}, {amount}. I have looked at the invoice and cannot find the reason. Please advise.

Scrooge

Mr Cratchit,

The entry {ref} for {what} is {amount}. I would like to know if it could have been less.

Scrooge

Bob,

Query on {ref}: {amount}. If that is the proper price, say so. If not, say why not.

Scrooge
replies:
Dear Mr Scrooge,

I have checked {ref}. The amount is correct as invoiced, {amount}. I am very sorry if it is more than expected. I have attached the paperwork to the entry.

Bob

Mr Scrooge,

I looked again and {ref} is right: {amount} for {what}. I'll note the reason on the entry so it isn't asked twice.

B. Cratchit

Dear Mr Scrooge,

Yes, {amount} is what was charged. I think it is fair, but I will ask the supplier whether they can do better next time.

Bob Cratchit

Mr Scrooge,

I have gone through it line by line. {ref} stands. I hope that is satisfactory.

Bob
